analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation row in docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 413). It documents a new environment variable, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP. The row describes a load-time shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots: a 128-token shader-cache probe runs twice, only a cold cache runs the shape cells, the budget is 20 seconds per engine, no rate or counter is trained, and the variable is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The supplied base units show only the surrounding base text, so the head line itself is cited only through the patch excerpt.

I saw no source changes, so no authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or coordinator-protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The warmup is described as a performance-only, excluded load-time step. It does not touch A-001 prompts, keys, attestation, or prefix-cache storage and encryption (T-041). The 'always' and 'off' values only affect startup latency.

Unverified contract: the implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift is not supplied. Whether warmup uses synthetic inputs only, never real consumer data, and never writes persistent shader or cache artifacts in a way that creates an at-rest leak is therefore unconfirmed. The doc states it trains no rate or counter and is excluded. The LaunchAgent passthrough allow-list gains one benign tuning variable; the Swift allow-list change is not visible here. The next pass should check that the source matches the doc if the code is in a batch.

No canonical threat model entries need updating from this doc-only change. The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), but the range map is complete and shows a single added line.
